- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (e.g., >0.67) and underperform when sentiment is bearish (e.g., <0.40), especially in early forecast periods.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% if sentiment turns neutral or slightly bearish within 3–5 days.
- Underreact to sustained bullish sentiment; if sentiment remains >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days, increase forecast mean by 2–5% to avoid mean reversion bias.
- Lag in downward corrections: if true price drops after forecast peak, delay correction by 1–2 days unless sentiment turns negative.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, cap forecast growth at 3–5% above prior peak to prevent over-optimism.
- For sentiment >0.80, reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to avoid overconfidence-driven overestimation.
- If sentiment drops below 0.20, reduce forecast mean by 3–5% to reflect risk aversion, especially if price has been rising.
